svg.aria-label: How to write ગ — એ — ખ — ઉ: 4 letters, ગ, એ, ખ, ઉ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ગ — એ — ખ — ઉ
svg.desc: 4 letters written one after another: ગ, એ, ખ, ઉ (gujarati). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ગ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ગ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; એ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, એ animation, first through third SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ખ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ખ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ઉ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઉ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: ગ: The teaching app animates ગ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left, circles clockwise around the rounded body, and finishes at the lower left. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the full right spine before turning through its lower foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded left body and tall right spine, but its printed body is broader and the spine foot more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's rounded-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, spine, and terminals differently. એ: The teaching app animates એ as three ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path circles the left bowl, flows through the broad lower body, and finishes through the small right arch at its junction. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate full-height right stem before curving through the lower foot. It lifts again and its third SVG path sweeps the separate high arcing mark from left to right. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the joined left bowl, lower body, small right arch, full-height right stem, and separate high arc, but its printed body is wider, its joins more angular, and its arc shorter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem-before-high-arc order and two-lift evidence while fitting all three runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, stem, foot, and arc differently. ખ: The teaching app animates ખ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left, descends through the left lobe, curls through the middle, and finishes beside the right spine. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the full right spine before turning through its lower foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the left lobe, inner curl, and tall right spine, but its printed lobe is broader and the spine foot more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's joined-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the lobe, curl, spine, and terminals differently. ઉ: The teaching app animates ઉ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins near the upper-left, circles clockwise through the small upper bowl to a narrow middle cusp, continues right and around the broad lower bowl, then climbs around the tall outer-left curve and finishes at the upper right without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper bowl, middle cusp, broad lower bowl, and tall outer curve, but its printed body is wider and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-bowl-to-lower-bowl-to-outer-curve order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the motion to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the bowls and terminal differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 letters, one after another
Letter 2 of 4 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 4 movements
Letter 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ગ animation, first and second SVG paths
Letter 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, એ animation, first through third SVG paths
Letter 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ખ animation, first and second SVG paths
Letter 4: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઉ animation, first SVG path
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
